# m.stocks.last_trade

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The latest trade of each US-listed stock.

Call it from a session `m`, made with `dm.MassiveSession()`:

```python
m.stocks.last_trade(symbols, *, on_error=None)
```

- [Methods](README.md#query-methods): `fetch()`, `poll(interval)`
- Read from: REST
- `poll()` by default: `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`, which holds only the latest poll's rows, one row per `Symbol`
- `poll(interval, mode=dm.PollMode.APPEND)`: appends each new state of a row, identified by `Symbol` and `Timestamp`

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows its rule under [shared arguments](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`symbols`](README.md#symbols) | Stock tickers. `dm.ALL` is refused; use `m.stocks.snapshots(dm.ALL)` for every ticker. |
| [`on_error`](README.md#on_error) | What a bad symbol or row does in this call (`dm.ErrorPolicy`). |

## Plans

How recent the data is on each of Massive's plans, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Last Trade (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Stocks Basic | Not included |
| Stocks Starter | Not included |
| Stocks Developer | 15-minute delayed |
| Stocks Advanced | Real-time |
| Stocks Business | Not included |
| Stocks Business + Expansion | Real-time |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The row's instrument, as Massive's ticker. From REST `T`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under." |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the row, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the New York date of `Timestamp`. |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's event time. From REST `t`: "The nanosecond accuracy SIP Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the SIP received this message from the exchange which produced it." |
| `Price` | double | The price of the trade. This is the actual dollar value per whole share of this trade. A trade of 100 shares with a price of $2.00 would be worth a total dollar value of $200.00. |
| `Size` | double | The size of a trade (also known as volume). |
| `Conditions` | long[] | A list of condition codes. See Stocks Condition Codes (https://massive.com/docs/rest/stocks/market-operations/condition-codes) for what each code means. |
| `Correction` | long | The trade correction indicator. |
| `Exchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/stocks/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. |
| `Id` | String | The Trade ID which uniquely identifies a trade. These are unique per combination of ticker, exchange, and TRF. For example: A trade for AAPL executed on NYSE and a trade for AAPL executed on NASDAQ could potentially have the same Trade ID. |
| `ParticipantTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond accuracy Participant/Exchange Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the trade was actually generated at the exchange. |
| `SequenceNumber` | long | The sequence number represents the sequence in which message events happened. These are increasing and unique per ticker symbol, but will not always be sequential (e.g., 1, 2, 6, 9, 10, 11). |
| `Tape` | long | There are 3 tapes which define which exchange the ticker is listed on. These are integers in our objects which represent the letter of the alphabet. Eg: 1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C. * Tape A is NYSE listed securities * Tape B is NYSE ARCA / NYSE American * Tape C is NASDAQ |
| `TrfId` | long | The ID for the Trade Reporting Facility where the trade took place. |
| `TrfTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond accuracy TRF(Trade Reporting Facility) Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the trade reporting facility received this message. |
| `DecimalSize` | String | The size of the trade including the fractional component. This is represented as a decimal string. |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, by the local clock. Rows that arrive together share it. It isn't Massive's time, and later rows can carry earlier times. In a `poll()` table, it's the time of the poll the row's values came from. |
